title: Concurrent duplicate creates can leak a database IntegrityError instead of 409

evidence.quote: url: str = Field(index=True, unique=True, description="Feed URL")

reasoning: create_feed implements duplicate detection as a pre-insert SELECT followed by an INSERT/COMMIT, while the schema enforces URL uniqueness at the database layer. Two concurrent POST /api/feeds requests with the same new URL can both observe no existing row; one commit succeeds and the other hits the unique constraint. Because the handler does not catch the commit-time IntegrityError, the loser can return a 500 instead of the route's documented 409 duplicate-feed response.
reproduction: Send two POST /api/feeds requests concurrently with the same new URL against a database that enforces the feeds.url unique constraint. The second transaction can fail during session.commit() after passing the existing-row check.
recommendation: Keep the pre-check for the common path, but also catch sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError around session.commit(), roll back the session, and translate feed URL unique-constraint failures to the same 409 response. Alternatively perform an atomic insert/upsert pattern appropriate for SQLite.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test only creates a single feed once; it does not cover duplicate creates or concurrent create requests.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a duplicate-create test that verifies the second POST /api/feeds returns 409, and ideally a concurrency test or unit-level simulation that forces commit to raise IntegrityError and verifies rollback plus 409.
minimumFixScope: app/api/feeds.py commit error handling in create_feed plus duplicate/IntegrityError coverage in tests/test_feeds.py.
